Re: LD 1090, Resolve, to Form a Working Group to Address Vacancies in Municipal Government Management Positions
Dear Members of the State and Local Government Committee:
On behalf of the Maine County Commissioners Association, we appreciate the opportunity to provide testimony to the Committee in support of LD 1090. We support the formation of a working group to address the important workforce challenges confronting local government, and we would further request that the legislation may be expanded to include county government on the working group.
About MCCA. Briefly, the Maine County Commissioners Association was established in 1890 to assist Maine's county government in providing vital services to Maine citizens in a responsive, efficient, and credible manner. The Association is based in Augusta, represents all 16 of Maine's counties, and is governed by a board with representation from each participating county.
What does LD 1090 do? This resolve seeks to establish a working group under the Department of Economic and Community Development to study and advise on the challenges faced by municipal governments in recruiting, retaining, and developing management employees.
Discussion. We recognize the critical role that effective management plays in the functioning of local governments. We are aware of the numerous vacancies in local government management positions across the state, which pose significant challenges to local governance and the delivery of essential services. We support strengthening local governments and ensuring they have the leadership necessary to serve their communities effectively.
While the focus of LD 1090 is on municipal government management positions, it is important to acknowledge that county governments are also part of Maine's local government ecosystem. Moreover, like municipalities, counties face similar challenges in workforce recruitment, retention, and development. Therefore, we respectfully request that the working group be expanded to include representatives from county government. This inclusion would allow for a comprehensive analysis of workforce issues at both the municipal and county levels, fostering collaboration and the sharing of best practices.

MCCA Letter re LD 1090 March 31, 2025 Page 2
We stand ready to assist in addressing the workforce challenges faced by local governments. We believe that our involvement in the working group would provide valuable insights and resources, contributing to the development of effective strategies to attract and retain qualified management personnel in both municipal and county governments.
Conclusion. We fully support LD 1090 and its objective to form a working group to address vacancies in municipal government management positions. We urge the Committee to consider expanding the scope of the working group to include county government representation, ensuring a holistic approach to workforce development in local governance. If you have questions or need additional information, please do not hesitate to let us know.
Respectfully submitted,

Stephen Gorden Co-Chair, Legislative Policy Committee, MCCA MCCA

Jean-Marie Caterina Co-Chair, Legislative Policy Committee,

Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association

Neither For Nor Against

LD 1090 - Resolve, to Form a Working Group to Address Vacancies in Municipal Government

Management Positions

March 31,2025

.

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and members of the State and Local Government
Committee, my name is Rebecca Lambert, and I am providing testimony neither for nor against LD 1090 on behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's (MMA) elected 70-member Legislative Policy Committee
(LPC). For reference, MMA is a nonpartisan, nonprofit member service organization and aims to help
provide policy solutions that work for all residents in Maine and the LPC guides the advocacy efforts and establishes positions on bills of municipal interest.
In the current municipal management climate, local leaders have increasingly become the proverbial punching bag for some members in their communities. This lack of discourse towards town and city managers has become one ofthe biggest challenges of enticing people into the profession and is part
of the reason for the lack of municipal managers entering the workforce today.
This hesitancy to be in the line of fire, coupled with the lack of a dedicated municipal management
post-secondary program are both major factors that are contributing to the workforce challenges municipalities are seeing today. Likewise, fewer individuals in the workforce are staying with the same employer for long periods of time. For municipal government, in years past this commonly looked like a
clerk working their way up through the ranks and that simply is not happening as much as it used to.
Local leaders appreciate the intent of LD 1090 in that it seeks to address a problem that municipalities across Maine are experiencing, but they are also cognizant of tight budgets and question whether this is the best use of resources to tackle the problem. Instead, municipal leaders believe that the Legislature should focus its attention on the element in Rep. Rollins' legislation which speaks to the
need for the return of public management and administrative courses in our public post-secondary institutions. Ensuring that future municipal leaders have the tools and skills necessary to manage an increasingly more complex role is a stepin the right direction and one that municipal officials strongly
support.
Thank you for your time and for considering the municipal perspective on this issue.
